sentences.text: Argochampsa possessed a long, narrow snout that made up about 70% of its skull, suggesting it lived a marine lifestyle.
Its upper jaw held five teeth in each premaxilla and twenty-six teeth in each maxilla.
Additional fossils recovered include the lower jaw, neck and back vertebrae, upper arm, and armor.
The genus was described by Hua and Jouve in 2004, and the type species A. krebsi honors Bernard Krebs.
The genus is based on a nearly complete skull found in the Oulad Abdoun Basin near Khouribga, Morocco.
Concave depressions on the lacrimal and prefrontal bones indicate the presence of salt glands.
The Paleobi Database classifies Argochampsa under the parent group Gavialidae.
Argochampsa lived in Morocco during the Paleocene epoch.
The time range for Argochampsa spans from the Danian to the Ypresian, between 66 and 48.07 million years ago.
